nodes.label: Full-Stack Context Inspection Rule
nodes.rationale: Always inspect both backend/ and frontend/ before developing features or bugfixes, to understand full context and avoid duplication. Rationale: features spanning both tiers drift in API shape, types and naming unless data flow is traced through both folders first; reuse is preferred over new endpoints/components/types.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS + Catalyst UI Styling Mandate
nodes.rationale: All UI must use Tailwind CSS for styling and Catalyst UI for core component structure, to maintain visual consistency and code quality. Deviations are allowed only with a strong reason documented in the code.
nodes.norm_label: tailwind css + catalyst ui styling mandate

nodes.label: Structured Logging Policy
nodes.rationale: Bare console.log/console.error are banned; use a leveled logger (winston/pino on Node backend, @sentry/browser or loglevel on frontend) centralized in a shared module such as /lib/logger.js. Rationale: ad hoc logging leaks sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII), loses level semantics, and cannot be configured per environment.

nodes.label: Shared Library Extraction Rule
nodes.rationale: Complex or widely useful logic must be extracted into a shared lib/utils directory (e.g. /frontend/src/lib) rather than embedded in deeply nested components or backend routes, so it can be imported instead of duplicated.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider AI Abstraction (ai-provider.js)
nodes.rationale: A single provider-agnostic AI layer fronts OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, selected by the AI_PROVIDER env var, so providers can be switched without code changes. OpenAI gpt-4o-mini is the default for fast/cost-effective resume parsing and quick matching; Anthropic claude-3-haiku is reserved for detailed analysis and complex matching. EMERGENT_LLM_KEY acts as a universal key across all three.

nodes.label: Resume Parser Service (AI Services Guide)
nodes.rationale: Uploads PDF/DOCX and extracts structured data (name, skills, experience, education) with AI to auto-populate the candidate profile. Parsed resumes are cached in the database and large files should be processed in background worker queues.

nodes.label: Job Scraper Service (AI Services Guide)
nodes.rationale: Scrapes Indeed (active) with LinkedIn/Glassdoor as placeholders pending API integration. Jobs are deduplicated on a unique externalId. MAX_JOBS_PER_SCRAPE caps volume because Indeed rate-limits and blocks; recommendation is scheduled cron scraping, caching and proxy rotation rather than real-time scraping.

nodes.label: Job Matcher Service (AI Services Guide)
nodes.rationale: AI compares candidate skills vs job requirements, experience level and location to return a 0-100 match score with matched skills, missing skills and reasoning. Matching costs 2-5s per job, so results are cached in the DB, batch endpoints exist, and cheaper models are used for initial filtering with complex models reserved for final matching.

nodes.label: Cover Letter Generator
nodes.rationale: Auto-generates a personalized cover letter per application from candidate profile plus job info; the user can review/edit it before submission.

nodes.label: Application Agent / Auto-Apply
nodes.rationale: Auto-applies to jobs whose match score exceeds MIN_MATCH_SCORE_FOR_AUTO_APPLY. Disabled by default (AUTO_APPLICATION_ENABLED=false) and gated by explicit user opt-in, complete profile, a daily cap (MAX_APPLICATIONS_PER_DAY) and application deduplication — these are deliberate safety brakes on an agent acting on the user's behalf. Should run as a scheduled batch job, not real-time.

nodes.label: Auto-Apply Safety Gates
nodes.rationale: Five layered constraints prevent runaway automated applications: complete-profile requirement, explicit user enablement, daily application limit, match score threshold, and deduplication. Master switch defaults to off.

nodes.label: AI Service Deployment Split (Monolith vs Microservices)
nodes.rationale: Current deployment is monolithic (Frontend <- Backend-with-AI <- MongoDB). Recommended at scale is an API Gateway fronting separate Auth/Job/AI/Application services so the AI service can be scaled independently, since AI matching is the slow, cost-dominant path.
nodes.norm_label: ai service deployment split (monolith vs microservices)

nodes.label: API Key Management Policy
nodes.rationale: Never commit API keys. Use environment variables, gitignored .env files, and secret managers in production; rotate keys regularly and never share dev/prod keys.

nodes.label: Production Security Checklist
nodes.rationale: Before production: strong JWT_SECRET, HTTPS only, secure cookies, rate limiting, sanitized uploads, CSRF protection, input validation, secrets in env vars, MongoDB auth enabled, restricted CORS origins.

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Authentication Scheme
nodes.rationale: Most endpoints require a JWT passed as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Token is issued by the OAuth callback and stored client-side.

nodes.label: API Rate Limits
nodes.rationale: Per-resource quotas reflect cost and abuse risk: resume parsing 10/hour, job scraping 5/hour (external site rate limits), AI matching 100/hour, auto-apply 1/day per user.

nodes.label: Emergent Preview Environment Base URL
nodes.rationale: The app has two API base URLs: local http://localhost:8000/api and a hosted preview at the emergentagent.com preview host. OAuth redirect URIs must be registered per environment.

nodes.label: Application Status Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Valid application statuses are pending, submitted, reviewing, interviewed, rejected, accepted — a candidate-facing funnel distinct from the agent's internal QUEUED/PROCESSING/COMPLETED/FAILED queue states.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Local Stack
nodes.rationale: Three containers — jobocate-mongodb (27017), jobocate-backend (8000), jobocate-frontend (3000) — brought up with `docker-compose up --build`. Source is bind-mounted so hot reload works for both tiers with no rebuild; MongoDB data persists in a named Docker volume by design, and `down -v` is the documented reset.

nodes.label: OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Google OAuth must have http://localhost:8000/api/auth/google/callback as an authorized redirect URI and localhost:3000/8000 as JS origins. Changes take 5-10 minutes to propagate at Google, which is why the mismatch error commonly appears immediately after configuring — remedy is wait, clear cache, or use incognito.

nodes.label: MongoDB Container Management & Backup
nodes.rationale: mongosh is reached via `docker-compose exec mongodb mongosh jobocate`; backup/restore use mongodump/mongorestore with --archive piped through exec -T.

nodes.label: Local Setup Checklist
nodes.rationale: Ordered onboarding path: install Docker Desktop, register Google OAuth redirect URIs, optionally configure LinkedIn, run ./start.sh or docker-compose up --build, then verify login at localhost:3000/login.

nodes.label: Service Health Verification Steps
nodes.rationale: Success is defined by four observable signals: frontend at :3000, backend /api/health returning {status:ok}, MongoDB connected per backend logs, and Google sign-in creating a user and landing on the dashboard.

nodes.label: pnpm Monorepo Layout
nodes.rationale: backend (NestJS), frontend (Next.js Pages Router) and packages/contracts are pnpm workspaces sharing tsconfig.base.json. Requires Node 20+ and pnpm 9+. Root scripts (pnpm dev / build / test / db:seed / typecheck) fan out across workspaces.

nodes.label: NestJS Backend Architecture
nodes.rationale: Module-per-domain NestJS API (auth, billing, entitlement, schemas, scripts) on port 8000 with Swagger docs at /api/docs. This supersedes the earlier Express server.js architecture described in PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md and AI_SERVICES_GUIDE.md.

nodes.label: Entitlement System
nodes.rationale: Feature gating by subscription plan expressed declaratively via the @RequireEntitlement decorator plus EntitlementGuard, rather than imperative plan checks in each handler. Three entitlement kinds — boolean (on/off), limit (usage counter with monthly reset, incrementUsage:true), and tier (hierarchical requiredValue) — cover all gating cases. Adding one means editing seed.ts and re-running pnpm db:seed.

nodes.label: @RequireEntitlement Decorator
nodes.rationale: Declares featureKey, optional incrementUsage and requiredValue on a controller method; enforced at request time by EntitlementGuard alongside JwtAuthGuard.

nodes.label: EntitlementGuard
nodes.rationale: NestJS guard that reads @RequireEntitlement metadata, checks the user's plan entitlement, and increments usage counters when configured.

nodes.label: Subscription Plan Tiers
nodes.rationale: Four tiers gate escalating automation: Free $0 (5 applications/month, 1 resume), Pro $29 (AI features, 50 applications/month), Elite $99 (human agent, unlimited applications), Interview $149 (dedicated coach, interview prep).

nodes.label: Stripe Billing Integration
nodes.rationale: Products/prices live in the Stripe Dashboard; the backend exposes checkout, portal, cancel and a webhook at POST /api/billing/webhook handling checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, and invoice.payment_succeeded/failed. Subscription state is driven by webhooks rather than polled.

nodes.label: JWT Access/Refresh Token Flow
nodes.rationale: Short-lived access token (15 min) in an httpOnly cookie plus a 7-day refresh token. Short access-token TTL limits blast radius of theft; httpOnly storage blocks XSS exfiltration. Note this conflicts with OAUTH_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md, which describes the JWT being stored in localStorage.

nodes.label: Google OAuth Preview Configuration
nodes.rationale: OAuth client ***REMOVED-GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID*** must list the preview host's /api/auth/google/callback as an authorized redirect URI and the preview origin as a JS origin. FRONTEND_URL/GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI on the backend and REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL on the frontend must all agree, otherwise CORS or redirect_uri_mismatch results.

nodes.label: LinkedIn OAuth Configuration (Optional)
nodes.rationale: Requires a LinkedIn app with the /api/auth/linkedin/callback redirect URI and 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' access; credentials go in backend .env as LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET. Optional — the platform ships with Google only.

nodes.label: /auth/success OAuth Callback Landing
nodes.rationale: After the provider authenticates, the browser lands on /auth/success which stores the JWT (localStorage per this doc) and forwards to the dashboard; the user record is created in MongoDB at this point.

nodes.label: @jobocate/contracts Shared Package
nodes.rationale: A single source of truth for Zod validation schemas, TypeScript types derived from them, and shared constants (FeatureKeys), consumed as a workspace dependency (file:../packages/contracts). Rationale: defining schemas once keeps frontend and backend in sync at both compile time (types) and run time (Zod parse), preventing the API/type drift the cursor rule warns about.

nodes.label: Contracts Build via tsup
nodes.rationale: tsup emits dist/index.js (CJS), dist/index.mjs (ESM) and dist/index.d.ts so both the NestJS backend and Next.js frontend can consume it. Editing a schema requires rebuilding (npm run build) or running watch mode (npm run dev) before consumers see the change — a common source of stale-type confusion.

nodes.label: FeatureKeys Constants
nodes.rationale: Exported from the billing schemas; supplies feature-flag identifiers such as AI_RESUME_OPTIMIZATION that the entitlement system gates on. Currently the only consumer in the codebase is backend/src/entitlement/__tests__.

nodes.label: Contracts Auth Schemas
nodes.rationale: RegisterSchema/RegisterDto, LoginSchema/LoginDto, TokenPayloadSchema/TokenPayload, UserRoleEnum, AuthProviderEnum and password reset schemas.

nodes.label: Contracts Billing Schemas
nodes.rationale: SubscriptionPlanSchema, UserSubscriptionSchema, FeatureKeys, PlanTypeEnum, SubscriptionStatusEnum and entitlement checking schemas.

nodes.label: Contracts User Schemas
nodes.rationale: UserSchema/User, UpdateUserSchema/UpdateUserDto, UserSettingsSchema/UserSettings, ExperienceSchema, EducationSchema.

nodes.label: AI Service Module (/src/ai-service)
nodes.rationale: Configurable AI provider support chosen explicitly for cost optimization — a unified interface over OpenAI/Anthropic/Google means the provider can be swapped by env var with no code change. Exposes parseResume, calculateJobMatch and generateCoverLetter.

nodes.label: Resume Parser Module (/src/resume-parser)
nodes.rationale: PDF/DOCX upload (5MB cap) -> validate and store (local or S3 via STORAGE_TYPE) -> extract text -> AI parse into structured data -> auto-update user profile. Dual local/S3 storage keeps local dev dependency-free while allowing encrypted S3 in production.

nodes.label: Job Scraper Module (/src/job-scraper)
nodes.rationale: Web scrapes Indeed with LinkedIn/Glassdoor ready for API integration; duplicates prevented via a unique externalId; rate limiting configurable per job board and robots.txt respected. Production guidance is to prefer official APIs over scraping.

nodes.label: ScrapedJob Schema
nodes.rationale: title, companyName, location, description, skills[], requirements[], salary, jobType, experience, source (LinkedIn|Indeed|Glassdoor), externalUrl, externalId (unique), isActive, scrapedAt. externalId uniqueness is the deduplication key across repeated scrapes.

nodes.label: Job Matching Module (/src/job-matching)
nodes.rationale: Computes match score with AI, tracks matched/missing skills and reasoning, supports marking interest, and generates recommendations. Persisting matches in the jobmatches collection makes the expensive AI call a one-time cost per user-job pair.

nodes.label: JobMatch Schema
nodes.rationale: userId, jobId, matchScore (0-100), matchedSkills[], missingSkills[], reasoning, isInterested, isApplied, matchedAt — the join entity between users and scraped jobs.

nodes.label: Application Agent Module (/src/application-agent)
nodes.rationale: Queue-based rather than synchronous: interest -> queue -> agent generates cover letter with AI -> ready for submission, with QUEUED/PROCESSING/COMPLETED/FAILED states, retryCount and batch processing on APPLICATION_AGENT_INTERVAL (30 min). Queueing decouples the slow AI generation from the user request and makes failures retryable. Disabled by default.

nodes.label: AgentApplication Schema
nodes.rationale: userId, jobId, status (QUEUED|PROCESSING|COMPLETED|FAILED), generatedCoverLetter, resumeUrl, queuedAt/processedAt/completedAt, errorMessage, retryCount, applicationData.

nodes.label: Extended User Schema (Candidate Profile)
nodes.rationale: Adds phone, skills[], experience[{company, position, duration, description}], education[{institution, degree, year}], certifications[] and resumeUrl so resume parsing can auto-populate the profile in place rather than in a separate entity.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Dependency Set
nodes.rationale: openai / @anthropic-ai/sdk / @google/generative-ai for AI; pdf-parse and mammoth for PDF/DOCX text extraction; axios + cheerio (+ optional puppeteer) for scraping; aws-sdk and multer-s3 for S3 storage; node-cron for scheduling.

nodes.label: Dual Local/S3 Resume Storage Strategy
nodes.rationale: STORAGE_TYPE switches between local filesystem (LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH) and S3 (AWS_REGION/ACCESS_KEY/SECRET/BUCKET). Local keeps dev setup trivial; S3 gives encrypted, durable storage in production. Uploads are constrained to 5MB and PDF/DOCX only.

nodes.label: Express Backend Layout (server.js)
nodes.rationale: Documents a Node/Express backend rooted at server.js (Express setup, MongoDB connection, Passport OAuth strategies, route mounting, error handling) with src/ subfolders for ai-services, resume-parser, job-scraper, job-matching, application-agent, models, routes and middleware. This description is superseded by the NestJS architecture in MONOREPO_README.md.

nodes.label: MongoDB Collection Model (Users/Jobs/JobMatches/Applications)
nodes.rationale: Four core collections: Users (auth ids, profile, skills, education, settings), Jobs (listing + scraping metadata + source), JobMatches (user-job join with score, skills gap, reasoning, interest flags) and Applications (candidate-job with cover letter, status, autoApplied flag, timestamps).

nodes.label: Environment Variable Contract
nodes.rationale: Required: MONGODB_URI, JWT_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and at least one AI provider key (OPENAI_API_KEY or EMERGENT_LLM_KEY). Optional: LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, AI_PROVIDER (default openai), JOB_SCRAPING_ENABLED, AUTO_APPLICATION_ENABLED.

nodes.label: Deployment & Scaling Considerations
nodes.rationale: Separate .env per environment with per-environment OAuth redirect URIs and CORS origins; HTTPS and MongoDB auth in production. Scaling levers: deploy AI services separately, Redis for sessions, API rate limiting, load balancing, CDN for static assets.

nodes.label: Next.js Frontend Layout
nodes.rationale: Pages Router with landing, login, signup, auth/success (OAuth callback), candidate and employer dashboards and pricing; src/ holds components (navbar/footer/common), AuthContext for auth state, assets and global styles. React 18 + Next 15 + Tailwind + Axios.

nodes.label: AuthContext (Frontend Auth State)
nodes.rationale: React context holding the authenticated user/JWT, consumed by pages behind login.

nodes.label: Jobocate Platform Overview
nodes.rationale: AI-powered job search app with Google/LinkedIn OAuth. Stack per README: React/Next.js + Tailwind frontend, Node/Express + Passport.js backend, MongoDB, JWT auth. Started via ./start.sh or docker-compose up --build; private and proprietary.

nodes.label: Resume Builder Redesign Summary
nodes.rationale: Replaces a basic form editor whose preview did not match the PDF with a FlowCV-inspired split-screen editor, real-time preview, 1s-debounced autosave and pixel-perfect PDF. Existing resume data, API compatibility, AI generate/regenerate, resume upload and the multi-step wizard are all preserved, so no migration is needed.

nodes.label: ModernResumePreview Component
nodes.rationale: Pure presentation component with exact A4 measurements, memoized for efficiency. Being pure and measurement-exact is what allows the same component to serve both the live preview and the Puppeteer-rendered PDF, guaranteeing they match.

nodes.label: ModernResumeEditor Component
nodes.rationale: Split-screen editor owning section editing, auto-save and state management; renders ModernResumePreview in the right panel.

nodes.label: Resume Preview Page (/resume/preview/[id])
nodes.rationale: Chrome-less page that renders the resume for Puppeteer to capture, accepting auth tokens for server-side rendering and signalling window.resumeReady when content and fonts are loaded.

nodes.label: Resume Builder PDF Generation Service
nodes.rationale: backend/src/resume-builder/resume-builder.service.ts drives Puppeteer to the preview page at a 1588x2246 viewport then prints A4 at scale 0.5 with printBackground and zero margins. The 2x viewport scaled down yields retina-sharp text; waiting on window.resumeReady plus a 1s font-render delay prevents capturing an unstyled page. PDF generation is inherently server-side only.

nodes.label: Pixel-Perfect PDF Matching Principle
nodes.rationale: The downloaded PDF must equal the on-screen preview exactly (WYSIWYG). Achieved by rendering the PDF from the same React preview component via a real browser (Puppeteer) rather than a separate PDF-drawing code path, which is what caused preview/PDF divergence in the old editor.

nodes.label: Debounced Auto-Save
nodes.rationale: Changes persist after 1s of inactivity; debouncing prevents an API call per keystroke while keeping work safe without an explicit save action.

nodes.label: Resume Template Design System
nodes.rationale: Customization axes: 6 color schemes (Blue/Green/Purple/Orange/Red/Indigo, each with primary/secondary/accent/dark/light variants), 3 font sizes, 3 spacing modes (Compact 1.4 / Normal 1.6 / Relaxed 1.8 line height) and 5 font families (Inter, Roboto, Playfair, Lato, Montserrat). Constraining to preset combinations keeps output professional and PDF-reproducible.

nodes.label: Resume AI Content Tools
nodes.rationale: Per-section Generate / Rewrite / Enhance actions covering summary generation, section regeneration, experience achievement bullets and skills extraction, exposed through /api/resume-builder/:id/regenerate-section.

nodes.label: FlowCV Design Inspiration
nodes.rationale: Design cites FlowCV (flowcv.com) for the split-screen editing model, plus Notion's clean interface, Linear's attention to detail, and Tailwind UI / Catalyst design systems.

nodes.label: Resume Builder Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)
nodes.rationale: Targets WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels on interactive elements, sufficient contrast, screen-reader friendliness, visible focus indicators, proper heading hierarchy and image alt text.

nodes.label: Resume Builder Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Planned: real-time collaboration, version history, live ATS score, template marketplace, multi-page resumes, Word/LaTeX/HTML export, custom sections, drag-and-drop reordering; plus dark mode and mobile touch optimization.

nodes.label: Split-Screen Editor Layout (Visual Guide)
nodes.rationale: ASCII wireframes of the editor: Content/Design tabs, left editing panel of collapsible section cards (Personal Info, Summary, Experience, Education, Skills, Projects) and right live-preview panel; the Design tab mutates colors/size/spacing/font with the preview updating in real time.

nodes.label: Editor UX Patterns
nodes.rationale: Five recurring patterns: collapsible section cards with header actions, click-to-edit inline fields with Save/Cancel, hover-revealed item card actions, a prominent 'Generate with AI' button per editor, and an auto-save indicator that shows 'Saving...' then 'All changes saved'.

nodes.label: Responsive Breakpoints
nodes.rationale: Desktop 1024px+ shows full split screen at 40% editor / 60% preview; tablet 768-1023px stacks editor above a collapsible preview; mobile <768px is single column with tabs to switch panes and touch-optimized controls.

nodes.label: PDF Generation Flow (Visual Guide)
nodes.rationale: Download PDF -> backend request -> Puppeteer launches -> navigate to /resume/preview/:id -> page signals ready -> capture A4 high-res -> save to server -> return download URL -> user downloads.

nodes.label: Editor Keyboard Navigation Map
nodes.rationale: Tab/Shift+Tab move between fields, Enter edits a section, Escape cancels editing, Space toggles a section, arrow keys navigate lists.

nodes.label: mongodb Compose Service
nodes.rationale: mongo:7.0 as jobocate-mongodb on 27017 with MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE=jobocate, a named mongodb_data volume for persistence, and a mongosh ping healthcheck (10s interval) that the backend gates on via depends_on: condition: service_healthy.

nodes.label: backend Compose Service
nodes.rationale: Built from backend/Dockerfile with root context, published on 8000, env from backend/.env.docker with AI/OAuth keys overridden from the host shell. Sets INTERNAL_FRONTEND_URL=http://frontend:3000 so Puppeteer reaches the frontend over the compose network rather than localhost. Anonymous volume masks /app/node_modules; backend-uploads persists resume files. Waits for mongodb to be healthy; HTTP healthcheck hits /health.

nodes.label: frontend Compose Service
nodes.rationale: Next.js dev server on 3000 with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL pointed at localhost:8000 (browser-side), WATCHPACK_POLLING=true so file watching works across the bind mount on macOS/Windows, and anonymous volumes shielding node_modules and .next.

nodes.label: INTERNAL_FRONTEND_URL Puppeteer Networking
nodes.rationale: Puppeteer runs inside the backend container, where 'localhost:3000' is the backend itself, not the frontend. INTERNAL_FRONTEND_URL=http://frontend:3000 resolves the frontend by compose service name so PDF generation can load /resume/preview/:id — distinct from the browser-facing REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL which must use localhost.

nodes.label: jobocate-network Bridge Network
nodes.rationale: Bridge network joining mongodb, backend and frontend, enabling service-name DNS resolution between containers.

nodes.label: pnpm Workspace Definition
nodes.rationale: Declares backend, frontend and packages/* as workspace members, which is what makes @jobocate/contracts resolvable as a local dependency from both apps.

nodes.label: Main/Testing Agent Communication Protocol
nodes.rationale: test_result.md is the single YAML-structured channel between the main agent and the testing agent, holding complete testing state and history. The main agent must update it (status_history, needs_retesting, test_plan, agent_communication) BEFORE invoking the testing agent, since the testing agent reads it to know what to test. stuck_count tracks repeat failures and is only reset once the testing agent confirms a fix — preventing premature declarations of success.

nodes.label: pdf-parse Import Bug (Resume Parser)
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL bug: resume parsing threw 'pdfParse.default is not a function' at resume-parser.service.ts:45 because pdf-parse v2.4.5 was imported as '* as pdfParse' and called via (pdfParse as any).default(buffer). Fixed by switching to a default import and calling pdfParse(buffer). Blocked all resume upload functionality; stuck_count 1, still marked needs_retesting.

nodes.label: Job Board Anti-Scraping Blockage
nodes.rationale: Indeed returns 403 Forbidden and LinkedIn is likewise blocked, so scraping returns 0 jobs even though the endpoints, error handling and DB integration work. Treated as expected behavior and documented in code; the testing agent's recommendation is to use official job board APIs instead of scraping for production.

nodes.label: Backend Test Sequence 1 Results
nodes.rationale: 7 backend services tested, 6 passing (85.7%). Passing: AI Service Integration, Indeed scraper, LinkedIn scraper, Job Matching, Application Agent, Authentication. Failing: Resume Parser (pdf-parse import). Email verification requires SMTP and was worked around for testing.

nodes.label: Emergent LLM Key Configuration
nodes.rationale: AI service runs on OpenAI GPT-4 via a single Emergent LLM key (a universal key spanning OpenAI/Anthropic/Google), verified as initializing the OpenAI client correctly. Note the key value is committed in plain text in test_result.md, contradicting the API key management policy in AI_SERVICES_GUIDE.md.

nodes.label: About Page (Figma-derived)
nodes.rationale: About page converted from Figma CSS to Tailwind at frontend/src/pages/about.js with hero, features and community sections. Initial breakage was an import error — Navbar and Footer are named exports, not default exports.

nodes.label: Jobocate Enhancement Problem Statement
nodes.rationale: Four goals: (1) About page matching Figma, (2) AI-powered resume processing that parses PDFs and auto-populates profiles, (3) job aggregation and matching from LinkedIn and Indeed, (4) user-driven application process where users mark jobs interested and an agent handles applications.

nodes.label: AppLoggerService
nodes.rationale: Implements NestJS's LoggerService interface so it can be dropped into NestJS's built-in Logger without changing call sites; context is set per-service via setContext() so logs can be traced back to the emitting module.

nodes.label: Daily Log Rotation with Compression
nodes.rationale: Files rotate daily at midnight and are gzipped, capped at 20MB each, with automatic deletion driven by LOG_MAX_FILES. Trade-off: bounded disk usage on long-running deployments at the cost of needing decompression to read history.

nodes.label: Structured JSON File Logging
nodes.rationale: Console output is colored and human-readable for development; file output is JSON with timestamp/level/message/context so logs can be machine-parsed by aggregators. Two formats for two different consumers.

nodes.label: Log Levels (error/warn/info/debug/verbose)
nodes.rationale: info is the production default and debug the development default, balancing signal against log volume and disk cost.

nodes.label: Never Log Sensitive Data Policy
nodes.rationale: Passwords, tokens, and PII must never be written to logs because file logs are retained for up to 30 days and shipped off-host, turning any leak into a durable one.

nodes.label: Express.js to NestJS Migration
nodes.rationale: The backend was converted from Express.js to NestJS to gain dependency injection, guard-based auth, interceptor-based uploads, exception filters, and DTO validation in place of ad-hoc middleware. Environment variables were deliberately left unchanged so deployment config did not have to move in lockstep.

nodes.label: NestJS Dependency Injection Pattern
nodes.rationale: Services are marked @Injectable() and injected via constructor rather than required at module scope, which makes them mockable in tests and lets NestJS own lifecycle.

nodes.label: Guards Replace Express Auth Middleware
nodes.rationale: Authentication middleware became guards applied with @UseGuards(), moving auth from a global chain to a declarative per-route/per-controller concern.

nodes.label: AI Services Module (AI Provider Service)
nodes.rationale: A single AI Provider Service abstracts both OpenAI and Anthropic so callers do not bind to one vendor.

nodes.label: Stub Modules Pending Implementation (Jobs, Matching, Applications)
nodes.rationale: Jobs, Matching, and Applications were stubbed rather than ported so the NestJS shell could ship first; the legacy JS services (job-scraper, job-matching, application-agent) still await TypeScript conversion.
nodes.norm_label: stub modules pending implementation (jobs, matching, applications)

nodes.label: JwtAuthGuard
nodes.rationale: Logs whether a Bearer token was present and surfaces TokenExpiredError / JsonWebTokenError distinctly, so a 401 can be attributed to a missing header versus an invalid signature without attaching a debugger.

nodes.label: JwtStrategy
nodes.rationale: Validates the JWT payload and re-looks-up the user in the database, which means a structurally valid token still 401s if the user was deleted — a deliberate trade of an extra query for revocation-on-delete.

nodes.label: JWT_SECRET Mismatch Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Tokens are signed with JWT_SECRET and validated with the same value, so rotating the secret invalidates every outstanding token; default JWT_EXPIRES_IN is 7 days.

nodes.label: Bearer Authorization Header Convention
nodes.rationale: Header must be exactly `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with a capital B and a space; the guard does a literal prefix match.

nodes.label: Practice / Consent / Live Notes Interview Modes
nodes.rationale: Three modes exist to separate consent postures around audio capture: Practice captures mic freely, Consent requires explicit permission confirmation plus a visible on-screen indicator, and Live Notes avoids audio capture entirely by having the user type questions manually. Mode gates which endpoints are legal.
nodes.norm_label: practice / consent / live notes interview modes

nodes.label: SessionContextBuilderService
nodes.rationale: Builds an immutable context pack from resume + job description + role so that coaching and scoring for a session are reproducible against a frozen snapshot rather than mutable profile data.

nodes.label: CoachingService
nodes.rationale: Generates structured coaching output with evidence anchoring; configured separately from scoring via LLM_INTERVIEW_COACHING_* env vars at a higher temperature (0.7) because coaching is generative.

nodes.label: ScoringService
nodes.rationale: Scores answers against a rubric; tuned via LLM_INTERVIEW_SCORING_* at a low temperature (0.3) because scoring must be consistent rather than creative.

nodes.label: InterviewBuddyService
nodes.rationale: Main orchestrator for the session lifecycle (CREATED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED), delegating to the context builder, coaching, and scoring services.

nodes.label: STTProvider Interface
nodes.rationale: Speech-to-text is abstracted behind an interface so development can run against MockSTTProvider without an OPENAI_API_KEY, selected at runtime via STT_PROVIDER.

nodes.label: Evidence Anchoring
nodes.rationale: Prevents the LLM from inventing claims about the candidate by requiring resumeAnchorsUsed[].evidence[] in coaching output, emitting factCheck.items[] with NEEDS_USER_CONFIRMATION when uncertain, and hard-blocking when hasBlockingIssues=true and the plan depends on unsupported claims. Chooses a false-negative (block) over fabricating resume content.

nodes.label: Zod Validation of LLM Outputs
nodes.rationale: All LLM outputs are parsed through Zod schemas shared from @jobocate/contracts (CoachingOutputSchema, ScoringOutputSchema, SessionContextPackSchema) so a malformed model response fails at the boundary rather than propagating into persisted turns.

nodes.label: PromptVersion (Versioned Prompt Templates)
nodes.rationale: Prompt templates live in a PromptVersion collection keyed INTERVIEW_COACHING_V1 / INTERVIEW_SCORE_V1 so prompts can be edited without a deploy; falls back to hardcoded defaults when a key is absent from the DB.

nodes.label: Interview Quota Enforcement (TODO)
nodes.rationale: Not yet implemented: should check plan entitlements before session creation and meter LLM/STT calls per session against subscription limits.

nodes.label: Catalyst UI Kit Changelog
nodes.rationale: Tracks Catalyst releases from the 2023-12-20 initial release through the 2025-08-13 swap of framer-motion for motion/react and the migration to Tailwind CSS v4 / React 19 / Next.js 15.4.

nodes.label: Migration from framer-motion to motion/react
nodes.rationale: As of 2025-08-13 Catalyst imports motion/react instead of framer-motion, following the upstream package rename; the README's install line correspondingly lists `motion` rather than `framer-motion`.

nodes.label: Data-Attribute-Based Transition API
nodes.rationale: Headless UI v2.1 replaced render-prop transitions with data-attribute-driven ones, so Dialog, Alert, and Listbox were rewritten and `as={Fragment}` was removed from transition components.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS v4 Upgrade Track
nodes.rationale: Catalyst tracks the latest Tailwind closely — v4.0 on 2025-01-23, then incremental bumps to v4.0.6, v4.0.15, v4.1.3 and v4.1.4 — which is why the kit assumes the newest Tailwind rather than pinning.

nodes.label: Catalyst UI Kit
nodes.rationale: A Tailwind CSS + React application UI kit from the Tailwind CSS team, shipped as copy-in component source (both TypeScript and plain JavaScript) rather than an installable package, so consumers own and can modify the components directly.

nodes.label: Catalyst Peer Dependencies (@headlessui/react, motion, clsx)
nodes.rationale: Components require @headlessui/react, motion, and clsx plus the latest Tailwind CSS; these are installed by the consuming project rather than vendored.

nodes.label: Tailwind Plus License (JavaScript Demo)
nodes.rationale: Grants Personal (one individual) or Team (up to 25 employees/contractors) rights to build unlimited End Products, but forbids redistributing components separately from an End Product or building anything competitive with Tailwind Plus. Governed by the laws of Ontario, Canada; liability capped at a refund of the license fee.

nodes.label: Personal License
nodes.rationale: Scoped to a single Licensee individual who may not share access; permits unlimited End Products for unlimited Clients including commercial SaaS and open-source projects.

nodes.label: Team License
nodes.rationale: Held by a business entity for up to 25 employees and contractors; adds the restriction that every End Product must be the sole property of the company or its clients, so staff cannot use the company license for side projects.

nodes.label: Non-Compete Redistribution Restriction
nodes.rationale: The core line is that components may not be re-distributed apart from an End Product, nor used to build website builders, starter kits, admin panel tools, or Figma/Sketch ports — anything letting an End User assemble their own products from the components would substitute for a Tailwind Plus purchase.

nodes.label: Catalyst Demo (JavaScript)
nodes.rationale: Plain-JavaScript variant of the Catalyst demo app; npm install then npm run dev, served on localhost:3000.

nodes.label: Tailwind Plus License (TypeScript Demo)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical duplicate of the JavaScript demo's LICENSE.md — the same Personal/Team terms are vendored into each demo variant so either can be distributed standalone.

nodes.label: Catalyst Demo (TypeScript)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript variant of the Catalyst demo app with identical run instructions to the JavaScript variant; the two demos exist so consumers can pick a language flavour.

nodes.label: Jobocate Claude Design Prompt Pack
nodes.rationale: An ordered pack of prompts for generating every remaining screen of the two-sided AI hiring marketplace in Claude Design. Prompts are pasted one at a time (each saving a .dc.html), preceded by a preamble, then handed back to Claude Code for a faithful port + backend wiring — separating design generation from implementation.

nodes.label: Base Preamble (Candidate + Marketing)
nodes.rationale: Pasted once per session to pin the design system so every generated screen matches existing .dc.html files exactly; carries tokens, fonts, card/button geometry, the dc document format, and the fictional universe (Sarah Chen, Stripe 96% match, coach Marcus Bell) so data is consistent across screens.

nodes.label: Jobocate Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Cream canvas #F7F3EA / surface #FFFEFB / ink #1B1A16 with brand green #1FA463, deep green #157A49, mint #5BD08C and clay #C9622E for warnings. Type: Instrument Serif for display, Hanken Grotesk for UI, JetBrains Mono for labels/metrics, Bricolage Grotesque 800 for the wordmark only.

nodes.label: Employer Preamble
nodes.rationale: The recruiter side reuses the same design system but swaps shell and accent: EmployerSidebar instead of AppSidebar, and indigo #4263EB as the recruiter primary identity while green stays reserved for positive/success and clay for rejections. Employer universe = Dana Whitfield at Stripe on the Growth plan.

nodes.label: Employer AI Addendum (Agentic Principles)
nodes.rationale: Employer AI features are agentic — the AI performs activity rather than reporting analytics. Every AI action must be TRANSPARENT (shows a why), REVERSIBLE (undo), and GATED (review-first by default, full-auto only as a per-rule opt-in), with idle/working/needs-approval status states and a ✦ sparkle + green #1FA463 visual language.

nodes.label: App Shell Pattern (Sidebar + Sticky Top Bar)
nodes.rationale: Logged-in screens share a flex root with a sticky AppSidebar import plus a main column carrying a translucent blurred top bar; marketing screens instead import SiteNav and SiteFooter. Two shells, one token set.
nodes.norm_label: app shell pattern (sidebar + sticky top bar)

nodes.label: EmployerSidebar (E0)
nodes.rationale: Must be designed first because every other employer screen imports it; mirrors AppSidebar's mechanics (collapse 250⇄74 persisted, mobile drawer, ⌘K palette, notifications) while swapping in recruiter nav groups HIRING/AI/ENGAGE/COMPANY and an AI-actions quota meter.

nodes.label: Employer Autopilot (EA1) — AI Recruiter Cockpit
nodes.rationale: Deliberately mirrors the candidate-side App Auto-Apply so the same mental model (master switch + editable rules + review queue + undoable activity log) serves both sides of the marketplace. Rules include auto-screen & rank, auto-advance ≥85%, auto-reject <50%.

nodes.label: Employer Copilot (EA2)
nodes.rationale: A conversational recruiting agent that executes rather than answers: replies render ACTION CARDS with Run/Edit/Undo plus a why, gated by an 'Always ask before acting' toggle.

nodes.label: Employer Sourcing Agent (EA3)
nodes.rationale: Autonomous sourcing plus AI-drafted personalized outreach that stays editable before send, with an outreach queue and campaign stats.

nodes.label: Employer Screening (EA4) — AI Auto-Screening Rubric
nodes.rationale: An editable weighted rubric derived from the JD and screening answers drives ranked applicant scores; every score expands to its reasoning, keeping the AI's ranking transparent and contestable.

nodes.label: Employer AI Interview (EA5)
nodes.rationale: Async AI-conducted screening interviews produce transcripts + competency scores + a recommendation; a second tab turns pasted notes/transcripts into a structured scorecard the recruiter confirms — AI drafts, human ratifies.

nodes.label: Employer Quota Reached (EC3) — Reusable Limit/Upsell State
nodes.rationale: One modal-able limit state is paired into Post Job, Sourcing, and Autopilot rather than reimplemented per surface; keeps an encouraging tone and always offers a non-purchase escape (Manage jobs / Close an old req).
nodes.norm_label: employer quota reached (ec3) — reusable limit/upsell state

nodes.label: Backend Modules Still To Build (Employer/Commercial)
nodes.rationale: Outstanding: job-postings, applicants/pipeline, interviews/scorecards, offers, org/teams+roles, billing/quota/entitlement, integrations, AI recruiter service, reporting/analytics. Candidate-side resume-builder, cover-letters, interview-buddy, matching and applications already exist.

nodes.label: Recommended Generation Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered candidate extras → account/system → employer (E0 first) → employer AI → commercial → marketing, because later screens import shells and reuse patterns established by earlier ones. Each group is handed back to Claude Code to import + implement + backend-wire before the next.

nodes.label: App States Reference Sheet (Y)
nodes.rationale: A single file rendering 404, generic error, empty list, offline/maintenance and loading-skeleton together, so reusable states are lifted from one canonical source rather than invented per screen.

nodes.label: Jobocate Next.js Frontend
nodes.rationale: Unmodified create-next-app boilerplate README; the app uses the Pages Router (pages/index.js, pages/api mapped to /api/*) and runs on localhost:3000.

nodes.label: Resume Template Preview Generation Guide
nodes.rationale: Two paths are offered — a Puppeteer-automated screenshot run (recommended) or manual per-card downloads from the HTML generator — so previews can be regenerated without designer tooling.

nodes.label: Adding a New Resume Template (4-Touchpoint Procedure)
nodes.rationale: A new template must be registered in four places that share the same template id: styles + markup in generate-previews.html, the TEMPLATES array in scripts/generate-all-templates.js, the templates array in src/pages/candidate/resume-builder/index.jsx, and the generated PNG. The id string is the coupling key across all of them.
nodes.norm_label: adding a new resume template (4-touchpoint procedure)

nodes.label: Template Image Specifications
nodes.rationale: PNG at 600x800 logical (1200x1600 at 2x) matching the resume aspect ratio, 50-200KB each; Next.js optimizes them at serve time and the builder falls back to placeholders when a file is missing.

nodes.label: Resume Template Images Folder
nodes.rationale: Holds the six preview PNGs served from /resume-templates/; the builder auto-falls-back to placeholders when an image is absent, so missing files degrade rather than break.

nodes.label: Six-Template Set (Modern, Professional, Creative, Minimal, Executive, ATS Friendly)
nodes.rationale: A fixed set of six named templates whose ids (modern, professional, creative, minimal, executive, ats-friendly) are the shared key between the HTML generator, the automation script, the PNG filenames, and the resume builder page.
nodes.norm_label: six-template set (modern, professional, creative, minimal, executive, ats friendly)

nodes.label: Resume Template Preview Generator Page
nodes.rationale: Renders all six templates as live styled DOM in a card grid so previews are authored in CSS rather than in a design tool; each card carries a Download button wired to downloadTemplate().

nodes.label: downloadTemplate()
nodes.rationale: Rasterizes a preview element to PNG via html2canvas loaded from a CDN, taking (elementId, filename) — the manual counterpart to the Puppeteer script's screenshot step.

nodes.label: generate-all-templates.js (Puppeteer Automation)
nodes.rationale: Launches headless Chromium (with --no-sandbox), loads generate-previews.html, screenshots each `{template-id}-preview` element at 2x, and writes PNGs to public/resume-templates/. Silently skips templates absent from the HTML, which is why a missing id shows up as a missing image rather than an error.
